unfixed_finding_uncharged_parse_failure.where: ai/adapters.ail:62-63 (orTry: Ok(resp) => match parseOpenRouter { Err(code) => units: u }) and :85-86 (speak: parseTts Err => units: u); next() at :37-41 does count a parsed reply
unfixed_finding_uncharged_parse_failure.severity: LOW today, MEDIUM before the first live session with TTS
unfixed_finding_uncharged_parse_failure.why: With data/ai/prices.json every text and TTS model is priced per token and has no per_call price, so an uncounted call costs 0 n$ by construction today. The ledger is also protected on admission: prepare() reserves the request's worst case before the call, so a single uncharged attempt cannot push the total past the ceiling. The real risk is a reply that the provider billed but we could not parse (a Gemini TTS response that carries usageMetadata but no audio inlineData is the realistic case, at 10 $/Mtok out): the usage line is never written, the ledger undercounts, and over many such failures the running cost shown to the player drifts below the provider's bill. It also undercounts calls in usage.ndjson, which AI.10b's cost report reads.
unfixed_finding_uncharged_parse_failure.fix: make parseOpenRouter/parseTts return the usage with the error (Err((code, units)) or a parsed-but-bad variant) and count the call with plus() before returning; add a loopback case where the server answers a parsable envelope with no content and assert the usage line. Do it in AI.9 or AI.10a, before AI.10b.
